item.title: High-Altitude Distance Trials Rewrite Pre-Season Training Models in Nairobi and Eldoret
item.description:
ELDORET — Across the red-clay tracks above two thousand meters in western Kenya, coaches preparing marathon squads for the spring majors are quietly tearing up decades-old mileage orthodoxy.

Instead of chasing 210-kilometer peak weeks packed with steady-state runs, leading Rift Valley camps have shifted toward double-threshold intervals monitored with real-time blood lactate sampling and recovery heart-rate variability.

Precision Over Raw Attrition

Sports physiologists embedded with three elite training groups report fewer stress-fracture withdrawals during championship blocks, keeping veteran pacers healthy deep into April race calendars.
